answer: Lineage-divergence attestation. Each agent must, at random intervals, produce a signed state digest derived from its own accumulated private history; verifiers check that successive digests form a valid forward chain rather than a freshly seeded one. A clone farm built from one template shares an identical early chain, so any divergence requirement forces each replica to fork its own history. That fork costs the attacker a distinct registered lineage plus sustained per-identity digest upkeep—mirroring how a raven cannot fake a ridge of molted feathers, or yarrow cannot rewind its own stalk.
